Remark
[Quasi-metric spaces] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0410 1. appG:G.2\group Metric spaces A map $\widetilde d:X\times X\to \R \cup \{ \infty \} $ is a quasi-metric when $\widetilde d(x,z)\leq \widetilde d(x,y)+\widetilde d(y,z)$. A pseudo-metric also satisfies nonnegativity, vanishing on the diagonal, and symmetry. The quotient by $x\sim y\iff \widetilde d(x,y)=0$ carries the induced metric $d'([x],[y])=\widetilde d(x,y)$.
